Oral Judgment:

1 This cross-objection has been preferred by the claimants against the judgment and award dated
5th March, 2009 passed by the learned Land Reference Court, District Latur in Lar No.543 of 1997.
2 The
learned Advocate for the claimants pointed out the pleadings, the evidence, the reasons and findings in the impugned judgment and the grounds of objections in the cross-objection.

He submitted that the claimants' land bearing Survey No.273, admeasuring 1 H 90 R i.e. 4 Acre 30 R,
was acquired for rehabilitation of earthquake-affected persons by notification dated 13th January,
1995, issued and published under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, "the said Act").
The award was passed on 29 th April, 1995.

The Land Acquisition Officer (for short, "LAO")
awarded the compensation at the rate of Rs.190/- per R i.e. Rs.7,600/- per Acre.
The learned Reference Court enhanced and awarded Rs.28,000/- per Acre.
He further pointed out oral and documentary evidence.

He pointed out the judgment of the learned Reference Court dated 19th July,
1988 passed in LAR No.1202 of 1992.
He pointed out that in the said judgment, the learned Reference Court 950 Cross-Objection-St-33295 of 2015.odt
has awarded Rs.32,000/- for non-irrigated land, Rs.40,000/- for seasonally irrigated land and Rs.48,000/- for irrigated land.
He submitted that the claimants' land is irrigated land.

He pointed out sale exemplar at Exhibit-19 executed on 11 th June, 1990, for consideration of Rs.1,55,000/-, for four Acre of land from Survey No.163/A/2 situated in one and the same village i.e. village Killari.
He, therefore, prayed to award the same rate of compensation to the claimants, as the said land is situated in the same area.
The sale exemplar is of the year 1990.
He also submitted that the said land is situated adjacent to Terna river and has a water pipeline and, therefore, acquired land is irrigated land.
He pointed out 7/12 extract of the claimants' land at Exhibits - 14 and 15.
The sugarcane crop is cultivated and harvested by the claimants and there are entries to that effect in the 7/12 extract.

In 7/12 extract Exhibit-15,
there is entry of well water.
He also pointed out the claimant's oral evidence in which he has stated that he was cultivating the said land and harvesting the sugarcane crop, which is not shaken in the cross-examination.
He prayed to award the enhanced amount of compensation.

3 The learned AGP for the respondents strongly opposed the cross-objection and submitted that the decision in LAR No.1202 of 1992, cannot be relied upon as the land of the claimant in the said 950 Cross-Objection-St-33295 of 2015.odt
case was acquired for the K.T. Weir.
The purpose of acquisition is different and it is acquired much earlier.
Thus, he submitted to not to rely upon that judgment.
He submitted to dismiss the cross-objection, as there is no substance in the grounds of objections of the cross- objection.

4 Perused the record and proceedings, particularly, the evidence, the grounds of objections of the cross-objection and the reasons and findings of the learned Reference Court in the impugned judgment.
The claimants land is irrigated land.
5 Sale exemplar Exhibit-19 is of highest value executed on 11th June, 1990 and the claimants' land was acquired by notification dated 13th January, 1995.
The judgment in LAR No.1202 of 1992 cannot be relied upon.

sentences.text: The said sale exemplar was executed five years earlier to the land acquisition process in question.
The claimants' acquired land is 4 Acre 30 R i.e. irrigated land.
However, for the small size of 0.60 R land and large size of the claimants land area i.e. 4 Acre 30 R land, a deduction of 20% is necessary and justifiable.
This 20% deduction comes to Rs.516/- per R.

If Rs.516/-
950 Cross-Objection-St-33295 of 2015.odt is deducted, then it comes to Rs.2067/- per R.

Therefore,
the claimants are entitled to the same rate of compensation as the market value of non-irrigated land i.e. Rs.2,583/- per R.
If it is multiplied by 10% cumulative escalation for five years, then the claimants are entitled for the enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs.3,437/- per R.

The learned Reference Court erred while determining the market value of the acquired land of the claimants and disbelieved the sale exemplar at Exhibit-19 without giving cogent and acceptable reasons.

Therefore,
interference is warranted in the impugned judgment and award.

The cross objection, therefore,
deserves to be allowed.
The impugned judgment and award deserves to be partly set aside.

Hence,
the following order:-
ORDER I.
The cross-objection is allowed.

II. The impugned judgment and award is partly set aside and modified as under:-
a) The claimants are entitled for the compensation at the rate of Rs.3,437/- per R for their acquired lands, including the earlier amount of compensation awarded and received by the claimants with additional 950 Cross-Objection-St-33295 of 2015.odt
components
i.e. solatium, interest and components
as per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
b) Rest of the judgment and award stands confirmed.
c) Award be drawn up as per the above modification.
III. If delay has been condoned by this Court while entertaining the cross-objection, the claimants shall not be entitled to interest for the said period of delay.
IV. The respondents are directed to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation alongwith statutory benefits and interest, in this Court within a period of six months from today.
V. If the court fees is not paid, on payment of court fees, the enhanced amount of compensation be paid to the claimants.
VI. Pending civil application, if any, is disposed of.
VII. Record and proceedings be sent back.
